honesty_banner: Prepared with AIC Server to help package an assessment. This is not an assessor decision and not an agency authorization. Gaps and unknowns stay listed. Security design follows NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5. CMMC packaging does not lower that bar. An assessor will decide Met after evidence review. This text alone does not mark a control Met.
architecture_boilerplate:
This binder describes the fixed AIC Server enclave model used for assessment packaging.

The control plane includes sign-in, privileged access, inventory, Current State Compliance, the Assessment Binder, disclosures, and Secure Share. Managed machines use agents when enrolled. Agentless discovery is used where supported. System Groups set sampling scope. Remote Access / Connect records operator sessions on assigned workstations.

Organization fields (legal name, CAGE, enclave name, MSP) fill this instance. They do not change the product model.

Typical deployments run in cloud infrastructure (AIC-operated or customer tenant). On-premises partner models may apply. AIC usually does not keep standing login access to customer hosts. Day-to-day work uses product roles, justifications, and evidence citations.

Cite live compliance scans, inventory, System Groups, Secure Share citations (titles and ids only - no CUI document bodies), Connect recordings, crypto status, disclosures, and retests. Do not treat this narrative alone as proof. Lab SoftHSM and demo passwords are not production claims.

First-pass packaging covers CMMC Levels 1 - 3 and related NIST SP 800-171 / 800-172 needs. NIST SP 800-53 remains the security design floor.

Cloud SKUs target FedRAMP and Microsoft GCC High postures where selected. This text does not claim a current FedRAMP ATO. Assessor sign-off lines stay blank in this tool. An assessor will decide Met after evidence review. This text alone does not mark a control Met.
fedramp_gcc_high_notes: Cloud offerings aim at FedRAMP and GCC High deployment postures. This binder does not claim that an Authorization to Operate (ATO) has already been granted.
iga_out_of_scope_label: Out of scope for this product pass - AIC Server does not deliver enterprise identity lifecycle (IGA) in this release. Describe below how this customer handles joiner / mover / leaver provisioning today.
readiness_pending: Section readiness will be computed at binder assembly.
floor_note: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 is the control design floor. CMMC / 800-171 / 800-172 are packaging overlays that reuse enclave evidence.
switch_effect: Switching the assessment standard remaps the punch-list and evidence view to that packaging overlay (which practices / control families are in scope). Enclave evidence already collected is reused and remapped - it is not wiped or re-collected.
attestation_default: The information in this package is accurate and complete to the best of my knowledge.

partner_netthunder.boilerplate: On-premises or partner-operated identity provisioning applies for this customer. The named partner operates directory / provisioning integrations. none_na.label: None / not applicable

cmmc.label: CMMC
cmmc.explanation: CMMC (32 CFR 170) is DoD assessment packaging over NIST SP 800-171 (and, at Level 3, selected NIST SP 800-172 enhanced requirements). Level 1 covers basic FCI safeguarding; Level 2 aligns to the 110 800-171 Rev 2 practices for CUI; Level 3 adds enhanced 800-172 requirements. CMMC does not replace the NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control design floor - it packages assessment evidence for a C3PAO / DoD review.

nist_800_171.label: NIST SP 800-171
nist_800_171.explanation: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 2 defines 110 security requirements in 14 families for protecting CUI in non-federal systems. Level 1 packaging focuses on basic / FCI-oriented practices; Level 2 is the full 110-practice set commonly paired with CMMC Level 2; Level 3 framing may reference additional enhanced expectations. Product control design still follows the NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 floor; 800-171 is assessment packaging over that floor.

nist_800_172.label: NIST SP 800-172
nist_800_172.explanation: NIST SP 800-172 (Feb 2021) adds 35 enhanced security requirements beyond 800-171. CMMC Level 3 selects a subset of these. This packaging view emphasizes enhanced requirements together with the underlying 800-171 / CMMC evidence. Unproven enhanced claims stay gap or unknown - switching here filters/remaps scope; it does not invent new host evidence.

nist_800_53.label: NIST SP 800-53
nist_800_53.explanation: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 is the control design floor for this product (moderate baseline, with High where selected). Control families (AC, AU, CM, IA, SC, SI, and others) organize the catalog. CMMC / 800-171 / 800-172 rows elsewhere are assessment packaging overlays that reuse the same enclave evidence - they are not a thinner substitute for the 800-53 floor.
